items.followUp: What is the difference between a client-server network model and a peer-to-peer network model?

rubric.why: Checks the basic meaning of a network model.
rubric.description: Defines a network model as a way of describing how computers or devices communicate over a network.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for describing a model of communication between networked devices.

rubric.why: Checks recognition of common network models.
rubric.description: Names a common model, such as client-server or peer-to-peer.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for naming at least one network model.

modelAnswer: A computer network model describes how computers or devices communicate and share resources over a network.
Common network models include client-server and peer-to-peer.
A network model describes how computers or devices communicate and share resources over a network.
Common network models include client-server and peer-to-peer.

items.followUp: Write any two characteristics of HTML.

rubric.why: Checks the fundamental nature of HTML.
rubric.description: States that HTML is a markup language used to structure web pages.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for identifying HTML as a markup language.

rubric.why: Checks a further characteristic of HTML.
rubric.description: States that HTML uses tags/elements and is interpreted by a web browser.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for mentioning tags/elements or browser interpretation.

modelAnswer: HTML stands for HyperText Markup Language and is used to create the structure of web pages.
It uses tags to mark up content, which a web browser interprets and displays.

items.followUp: What is the purpose of the <body> tag in an HTML document?

rubric.why: Checks the role of the html element in the document structure.
rubric.description: Identifies <html> as the root element that encloses the HTML document.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that it contains or encloses the complete document.

rubric.why: Checks that the tag marks the boundaries of the HTML document.
rubric.description: Explains that the opening and closing <html> tags mark the beginning and end of the HTML document.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for explaining the document boundaries.

modelAnswer: The <html> tag is the root element of an HTML document.
The opening <html> tag marks the start of the document, and the closing </html> tag marks its end.

items.followUp: List the steps you would take to determine the requirements before drawing a flowchart for calculating the average of three numbers.

rubric.why: Checks that the problem is understood before designing the flowchart.
rubric.description: Identify and understand the problem to be solved.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for mentioning problem identification or understanding.

rubric.why: Checks identification of the data the flowchart needs.
rubric.description: Determine the required input data.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for identifying the input.

rubric.why: Checks identification of the operations required.
rubric.description: Determine the processing or operations needed to solve the problem.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for identifying the processing or solution steps.

rubric.why: Checks identification of the expected outcome.
rubric.description: Determine the required output or result.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for identifying the output.

modelAnswer: Understand and clearly define the problem to be solved.
Determine the input data required.
Identify the processing steps or operations needed.
Determine the output or result required.

items.followUp: Explain any four advantages of using a computer network.

rubric.why: Checks an important practical reason for networking computers.
rubric.description: Explains that networks allow resources such as printers, software or storage to be shared.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating resource sharing with an example or clear explanation.

rubric.why: Checks the ability to share information between users.
rubric.description: Explains that users can share files or data across the network.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for mentioning file or data sharing.

rubric.why: Checks the role of networks in communication.
rubric.description: Explains that networks enable communication, such as email or messaging.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for mentioning communication and/or an example.

rubric.why: Checks an additional benefit of networking.
rubric.description: Explains a further benefit, such as centralized management/backup or access to the Internet.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for one valid additional benefit.

modelAnswer: Computer networks allow users to share resources such as printers, software and storage devices.
They make it easy to share files and data between connected computers.
They support communication through services such as email and messaging.
Networks can also provide centralized management and backup, and shared access to the Internet.

items.followUp: What is decryption, and how does it help protect information sent over the Internet?

rubric.why: Checks the definition of encryption.
rubric.description: Defines encryption as converting readable information (plaintext) into an unreadable coded form (ciphertext).
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for describing conversion of readable data into coded/unreadable data.

rubric.why: Checks recognition of the encrypted form of information.
rubric.description: Names or describes the encrypted information as ciphertext or coded data.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for identifying the result as ciphertext or coded/unreadable data.

rubric.why: Checks the main protection encryption provides.
rubric.description: Explains that encryption prevents unauthorized people from reading information and protects privacy/confidentiality.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for explaining protection from unauthorized access or privacy.

rubric.why: Checks application to everyday Internet use.
rubric.description: Gives a relevant everyday use, such as protecting passwords, personal information or online transactions.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for a valid everyday Internet example.

modelAnswer: Encryption is the process of converting readable information, called plaintext, into an unreadable coded form, called ciphertext.
Only someone with the required key can decrypt the ciphertext and read the original information.
Encryption protects the privacy of information and helps prevent unauthorized people from reading data sent over the Internet.
It is important for everyday activities such as protecting passwords, personal details and online transactions.

items.followUp: What does a connector symbol represent in a flowchart?

rubric.why: Checks what a flow line looks like and indicates.
rubric.description: States that a flow line is a line, usually with an arrow, connecting flowchart symbols and showing direction.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for identifying the line or arrow.

rubric.why: Checks the meaning of the flow line in a flowchart.
rubric.description: Explains that it shows the sequence or direction of control from one step to another.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that it shows the order or direction of steps.

modelAnswer: A flow line is a line, usually ending in an arrow, that connects symbols in a flowchart.
It shows the direction and sequence in which the steps are carried out.

items.followUp: How can the “Act it Out” strategy help in solving a problem?

rubric.why: Checks the basic meaning of the strategy.
rubric.description: States that Act it Out involves physically performing or simulating the actions in a problem.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for describing acting, role-playing or simulating the problem.

rubric.why: Checks the purpose of the strategy.
rubric.description: Explains that acting out the steps helps understand or solve the problem, or check the sequence of actions.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating a relevant purpose or benefit.

modelAnswer: “Act it Out” is a problem-solving strategy in which the actions or steps of a problem are physically performed or simulated.
This helps make the process easier to understand and can help find the correct sequence or solution.
